Loading the data¶

The full data cleaning process can be found in cleaning.ipynb in our GitHub Repository

attainment[year_cols] = attainment[year_cols].notna().astype(int)
attainment[attainment["st_abbr"].isin(rb_codes)]

def load_bea_data(file_path): 
    file = pd.read_csv(file_path)
    file["never_treated"] = (~file["GeoFIPS"].astype("string").isin(tr_counties)).astype(int)
    file = file[(file["GeoName"] == "Wayne, MI")|((file["never_treated"] == 1))]
    file["post"] = (file["year"] >= 2005).astype(int) # year in wich Wayne, MI was first assigned non-attainment status
    file["treated"] = (file["never_treated"] == 0).astype(int)
    file["D"] = file["post"] * file["treated"] # DID treatment indicator
    return file

gdp_tc = load_bea_data("gdp_components_rust_belt.csv") #GDP by county at industry level
income = load_bea_data("income_cleaned.csv") #personal income by county at industry level
output_index = load_bea_data("quant_index_cleaned.csv") #output quantity index by county at industry level

gdp_tc = gdp_tc.rename(columns={"All industry total": "gdp_all"})
gdp_tc["manufac_share"] = gdp_tc["Manufacturing"] / gdp_tc["gdp_all"]

We restrict the sample to "manufacturing hubs" defined as counties with (i) an average population of at least 500,000 in the pre-treatment periods of 2001 to 2004.

In [48]:
# pre_treat avg up to 2004
gdp_pre04 = gdp_tc[gdp_tc["year"] <= 2004]
inc_pre04 = income[income["year"] <= 2004]

#avg share of manufacturing gdp and avg population in pre-treatment period
avg_share = (
    gdp_pre04
    .groupby("GeoFIPS")["manufac_share"]
    .mean()
)

avg_pop = (
    inc_pre04
    .groupby("GeoFIPS")["Population (persons) 2/"]
    .mean()
)

# cutoffs of a "manufacturing hub"
hub_share_cutoff = avg_share.quantile(0.5)
hub_pop_cutoff = 500000
share_cut_off_counties = avg_share[avg_share >= hub_share_cutoff].index
pop_cut_off_counties   = avg_pop[avg_pop >= hub_pop_cutoff].index

#apply to full panel 
hubs_gdp = gdp_tc[gdp_tc["GeoFIPS"].isin(share_cut_off_counties)&gdp_tc["GeoFIPS"].isin(pop_cut_off_counties)]
hubs_gdp = hubs_gdp[hubs_gdp["year"]<= 2010]

hubs_income = income[income["GeoFIPS"].isin(share_cut_off_counties)&income["GeoFIPS"].isin(pop_cut_off_counties)]
hubs_income = hubs_income[hubs_income["year"]<= 2010]

hubs_output = output_index[output_index["GeoFIPS"].isin(share_cut_off_counties)&output_index["GeoFIPS"].isin(pop_cut_off_counties)]
hubs_output = hubs_output[hubs_output["year"]<= 2010]

print(f"The analysis will focus on the following counties: {hubs_gdp['GeoName'].unique()}")

# Data table of characteristics of the counties in the donor pool and treated unit
char_df = (
    avg_pop.rename("avg_population")
    .to_frame()
    .join(avg_gdp_all.rename("avg_gdp_all"))
    .join(avg_income_pc.rename("avg_income_pc"))
    .reset_index()
)

def summary_table(df, cols):
    donors = df[df["treated"] == 0]
    treated = df[df["treated"] == 1]

    rows = []
    for c in cols:
        rows.append({
            "Variable": c,
            "Wayne, MI": treated[c].iloc[0],
            "Donor Mean": donors[c].mean(),
            "Donor Median": donors[c].median(),
            "Donor 25th pct": donors[c].quantile(0.25),
            "Donor 75th pct": donors[c].quantile(0.75),
            "Wayne Percentile": (donors[c] < treated[c].iloc[0]).mean()
        })

    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

table_chars = summary_table(
    char_df,
    cols=["avg_population", "avg_gdp_all", "avg_income_pc"]
)

table_chars_fmt = table_chars.copy()

for col in ["Wayne, MI", "Donor Mean", "Donor Median", "Donor 25th pct", "Donor 75th pct"]:
    table_chars_fmt[col] = table_chars_fmt[col].apply(lambda x: f"{x:,.0f}")

table_chars_fmt["Wayne Percentile"] = table_chars_fmt["Wayne Percentile"].apply(
    lambda x: f"{100*x:.1f}%"
)

table_chars_fmt

As the Rust Belt is historically characterized by a strong presence of heavy industries like manufacturing, we can verify this by examining the region’s industrial composition. Understanding the sectoral structure of Wayne, MI allows us to gain deeper insight into the industrial dynamics that define the treatment county. We use 2004, the year preceding treatment, as the benchmark for this analysis.

While many broad industries can be further disaggregated into more granular subindustries (for example, durable goods within manufacturing, which we explore in later sections), we will focus on major industry groups. The classification of these main industry groups is based on county-level compensation data published by the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA).

wayne_2004 = gdp_tc[(gdp_tc["GeoName"] == "Wayne, MI") & (gdp_tc["year"] == 2004)].copy()

Next, we plot the paths of all-industry GDP, manufacturing component of the GDP, and the GDP quantity index between Wayne, MI and the never-treated counties

In [52]:
# GDP levels plots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5), sharex=True)

for ax, col, title in zip(
    axes,
    ["Manufacturing", "gdp_all"],
    ["Manufacturing GDP", "All Industries GDP"],
):
    for _, gdf in hubs_gdp.groupby("GeoFIPS"):
        ax.plot(gdf["year"], gdf[col], alpha=0.2, lw=1, color="k")
    wayne = hubs_gdp[hubs_gdp["GeoName"] == "Wayne, MI"]
    ax.plot(
        wayne["year"],
        wayne[col],
        label="Wayne County, MI",
        lw=2,
    )
    (
        hubs_gdp[hubs_gdp["never_treated"] == 1]
        .groupby("year")[col]
        .mean()
        .plot(ax=ax, label="Mean never-treated counties", lw=2)
    )
    ymax = ax.get_ylim()[1]
    ax.vlines(
        x=2005,
        ymin=0,
        ymax=ymax,
        linestyle=":",
        lw=2,
        label="Treatment (2005)",
    )
    ax.set_xlim(2001, 2010)

    ax.set_title(f"Wayne vs Never-treated: {title}")
    ax.set_xlabel("Year")
axes[0].set_ylabel("GDP (levels)")
axes[1].set_ylabel("")

axes[0].legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

plt.savefig(
    "gdp_levels_wayne_vs_donors.pdf",
    format="pdf",
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.close()

TWFE Model¶

The two-way fixed effect model estimates the dynamic effect of being assigned a nonattainment status on Wayne County's. For the post-treatment periord, we focus on 2005 to 2010.

In [54]:
model_df = hubs_gdp[['Manufacturing', 'gdp_all', 'D', 'year', 'GeoFIPS', "treated"]].dropna().copy()
model_df = model_df[model_df["year"] <= 2010]

model_df['gdp_m'] = model_df['gdp_all'] / 1_000_000
model_df['Manufacturing_m'] = model_df['Manufacturing'] / 1_000_000
In [55]:
# Overall Output
gdp_twfe = pf.feols(
    "gdp_m ~ i(year, treated,  ref = 2004) | GeoFIPS + year",
    model_df,
    vcov={"CRV1": "GeoFIPS"}, #clustered standard errors at the county level
)

gdp_twfe.summary()

gdp_twfe.iplot(
    coord_flip=False,
    figsize=(10, 5),
    yintercept=0,  
    cat_template="{value_int}",
    xintercept=2.5,
    title="Event study: Effect of Nonattainment Status on GDP (All Industries, Millions)",
)

Synthetic Control¶

For outcomes other than all-industry GDP, we see evidence suggesting the violation of parallel trend assumption. For these outcomes, we utilize a synthetic control setup. We approach this two ways: first by custom-coding the functions to compute synthetic controls and then using the scipi package for convenience.

X1 = inverted["Wayne, MI"].values               

X0_names = [c for c in inverted.columns if c != "Wayne, MI"]
X0 = inverted[X0_names].values              

def loss_w(W, X0, X1) -> float:
    scale = 1e8  
    diff = (X1 - X0.dot(W)) / scale
    return np.mean(diff**2)

def get_w(X0, X1):
    w_start = [1 / X0.shape[1]] * X0.shape[1]   
    weights = fmin_slsqp(
        partial(loss_w, X0=X0, X1=X1),
        np.array(w_start),
        f_eqcons=lambda x: np.sum(x) - 1,      
        bounds=[(0.0, 1.0)] * len(w_start),    
        disp=False
    )
    return weights

wayne_weights = get_w(X0, X1)


wayne_weights_series = pd.Series(wayne_weights, index=X0_names, name="weight")

In [63]:
# Function to compute synthetic control for any county in the panel
def synthetic_control(geofips: int, data: pd.DataFrame, treat_year: int):

    features = ["Manufacturing"]

    # Pre-treatment matrix for weights
    inverted = (
        data
        .query("year < @treat_year")
        .pivot(index="GeoFIPS", columns="year")[features]
        .T
    )

    # Treated vs donors
    y = inverted[geofips].values
    X = inverted.drop(columns=geofips).values

    weights = get_w(X, y)

    # Synthetic series for ALL years
    donor_panel = (
        data
        .query("GeoFIPS != @geofips")
        .pivot(index="year", columns="GeoFIPS")["Manufacturing"]
        .sort_index()
    )

    synthetic = donor_panel.values.dot(weights)   # length = number of years

    # Treated county rows for ALL years
    treated_rows = (
        data
        .query("GeoFIPS == @geofips")
        .sort_values("year")[["GeoFIPS", "GeoName", "year", "Manufacturing"]]
    )

    # make sure lengths line up
    if len(treated_rows) != len(synthetic):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Length mismatch: treated has {len(treated_rows)} rows, "
            f"synthetic has {len(synthetic)}."
        )

    return treated_rows.assign(synthetic=synthetic)

synthetic_control(26163, hubs_gdp, treat_year)

# Synthetic Control - Manufacturing Component of GDP in manufacturing hubs (using scpi_pkg)
# Keep only needed columns and drop missing outcome
df_use = hubs_gdp[["GeoFIPS", "year", "post", "never_treated", "Manufacturing"]].dropna(subset=["Manufacturing"]).copy()

# Candidate pool: treated + never-treated donors
df_use = df_use[(df_use["GeoFIPS"] == TREATED) | (df_use["never_treated"] == 1)].copy()

# Balance on pre-period (must have all pre years)
pre = df_use[df_use["year"].isin(period_pre)]
counts = pre.groupby("GeoFIPS")["year"].nunique()
good_units = counts[counts == n_pre].index

unit_co = np.array(sorted([u for u in good_units if u != TREATED]))

df_bal = df_use[df_use["GeoFIPS"].isin(good_units)].copy()

# standardzing the outcome 
mu = df_bal.loc[df_bal["year"].isin(period_pre), "Manufacturing"].mean()
sd = df_bal.loc[df_bal["year"].isin(period_pre), "Manufacturing"].std()
df_bal["y_sc"] = (df_bal["Manufacturing"])/1000 #dividing by 1000 due to the magnitude of the outcome variable

scdf = scdata(
    df=df_bal,
    id_var="GeoFIPS",
    time_var="year",
    outcome_var="y_sc",
    period_pre=period_pre,
    period_post=period_post,
    unit_tr=TREATED,
    unit_co=unit_co,
    features=["y_sc"],
    cov_adj=None,
    cointegrated_data=True,   
    constant=False
)

est = scest(scdf, w_constr={'p': 'L1', 'dir': '==', 'Q': 1, 'lb': 0})

w_constr = {'name': 'simplex', 'Q': 1}

u_sigma = "HC1"
u_order = 1
u_lags = 0
e_method = "gaussian"
e_order = 1
e_lags = 0
e_alpha = 0.05
u_alpha = 0.05
sims = 200
cores = 1

random.seed(8894)
result = scpi(scdf, sims=sims, w_constr=w_constr, u_order=u_order, u_lags=u_lags,
              e_order=e_order, e_lags=e_lags, e_method=e_method, u_missp=u_missp,
              u_sigma=u_sigma, cores=cores, e_alpha=e_alpha, u_alpha=u_alpha)
scplot(result, e_out=True, x_lab="year", y_lab="Standardized Manufacturing Output")

pre = sorted(rb_aqi_pmo.loc[rb_aqi_pmo["post"] == 0, "year"].unique().tolist())
post = sorted(rb_aqi_pmo.loc[rb_aqi_pmo["post"] == 1, "year"].unique().tolist())

unit_tr = "Wayne"
unit_co = sorted(rb_aqi_pmo.loc[rb_aqi_pmo["county"] != unit_tr, "county"].unique().tolist())


pmdf = scdata(df=rb_aqi_pmo, id_var="county", time_var="year", outcome_var="pm25_dm",
              period_pre=np.array(pre), period_post=np.array(post),
              unit_tr=unit_tr, unit_co=unit_co, features=["pm25_dm"], cov_adj=None,
              cointegrated_data=True, constant=False)

est_si = scest(pmdf, w_constr={'name': "simplex"})
print(est_si)

w_constr = {'name': 'simplex', 'Q': 1}
u_missp = True
u_sigma = "HC1"
u_order = 1
u_lags = 0
e_method = "gaussian"
e_order = 1
e_lags = 0
e_alpha = 0.05
u_alpha = 0.05
sims = 200
cores = 1

random.seed(8894)
result = scpi(pmdf, sims=sims, w_constr=w_constr, u_order=u_order, u_lags=u_lags,
              e_order=e_order, e_lags=e_lags, e_method=e_method, u_missp=u_missp,
              u_sigma=u_sigma, cores=cores, e_alpha=e_alpha, u_alpha=u_alpha)
scplot(result, e_out=True, x_lab="year", y_lab="Demeaned PM2.5 AQI")
